Cairn has been rebuilt around its new local-first, project-aware agent memory
architecture. **This release starts the new Cairn release line.** Previous v0.x
releases represented an obsolete implementation and have been retired.

This is the first release of the rebuilt Cairn, and it is an **alpha**.

## What Cairn does

Cairn gives a coding agent memory that survives the session. It watches what
actually happened in your repository — files changed, commands run, tests
executed, errors hit — and turns that into durable, scoped, traceable memory
that the agent gets back the next time it opens the project.

- **Local-first.** Capture, recall, context assembly, handoff and search all
  work with no network and no server. Remote sharing is an enhancement layered
  on top of a complete local system, never a requirement.
- **Project, branch, task and session scoped.** Every memory carries explicit
  scope and provenance back to the session and observations that produced it.
  Retrieval respects scope precedence, and anything recalled can be traced to
  where it came from.
- **Repository state comes from Git**, not from guesswork. Two clones of one
  repository at different paths resolve correctly.
- **Claude Code and MCP.** `cairn connect claude-code` installs the hooks and
  registers Cairn's MCP server. The daemon starts on its own; sessions open and
  close as you work.
- **Session continuity.** Handoffs are written at compaction, at session end,
  and on recovery — recording completed work, remaining work, decisions,
  failures, tests run, and the next step.
- **Context briefings** are assembled within a token budget, deterministically,
  degrading from the bottom instead of truncating arbitrarily.
- **Search** is lexical, over SQLite FTS5. No embeddings, no vector store, no
  index service to run.
- **Opt-in sync.** Link a project and its queued changes reach your Cairn
  server through a transactional outbox. Delivery is exactly-once in effect:
  rows are claimed before they are sent, and the server claims each idempotency
  key inside the transaction that applies the change, so a redelivery is a
  no-op rather than a duplicate or a spurious failure.
- **Web UI** for browsing projects, sessions, handoffs, tasks, memory and sync
  status without a terminal.

## The privacy boundary

This is structural, not a promise:

- Full conversations and raw tool output are **never persisted**. Captured
  payloads are bounded and summarized, and values matching common secret
  patterns are redacted before anything is written.
- Raw observation content **cannot be transmitted**. There is no observation
  entity type on the wire, so such a payload cannot be constructed. A memory or
  handoff carries evidence as identifiers and a count — not content.
- A project you have not linked produces **zero outbound requests** containing
  its data.
- You can exclude paths and commands, keep memory local-only, and delete any
  observation, memory or session.

## Supported platforms

| Platform | Status |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon, `aarch64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| macOS (Intel, `x86_64-apple-darwin`) | Supported |
| Linux (`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Linux (`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`) | Supported |
| Windows | **Not supported** |

Windows support is not implemented: the CLI and daemon communicate over a Unix
domain socket. No Windows artifact is published, and none should be inferred
from the retired release line.

## Install

Download the archive for your platform, verify it, and put the binaries on your
PATH. `cairn` and `cairnd` must live in the same directory — `cairn` starts the
daemon itself.

```bash
VERSION=0.1.0-alpha.1
TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin   # or x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu

curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/releases/download/v${VERSION}/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS

tar -xzf cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}.tar.gz
sudo install -m 0755 cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairn cairn-v${VERSION}-${TARGET}/cairnd /usr/local/bin/
```

Then, inside a Git repository:

```bash
cairn init
cairn connect claude-code
```

Building from source works too and needs nothing but the pinned toolchain:

```bash
cargo build --workspace --release
```

## Container images

Only the server-side components ship as images. The local agent is native by
design — running your editor's memory daemon in a container buys nothing.

```
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-server:0.1.0-alpha.1
ghcr.io/vellixia/cairn-web:0.1.0-alpha.1
```

Both are also published under an immutable `sha-<short-sha>` tag and built for
`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. There is deliberately no `latest` tag for a
pre-release. An example stack — PostgreSQL, server, web — is in
[`deploy/docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/blob/main/deploy/docker-compose.yml).

## Verifying what you downloaded

- `SHA256SUMS` covers every archive.
- `SBOM.spdx.json` describes the release contents.
- Archives and images carry GitHub build provenance attestations:

```bash
gh attestation verify cairn-v0.1.0-alpha.1-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz --repo Vellixia/Cairn
```

## Known limitations

- **Alpha.** Expect defects. Do not depend on this for anything you cannot
  reconstruct.
- **Pre-1.0 compatibility.** APIs, storage schemas and the wire protocol may
  change without a deprecation period before 1.0.0. There is no upgrade path
  from the retired v0.x line, and none will be provided.
- **No Windows support.**
- **Sharing requires your own server.** There is no hosted Cairn service.
- The web UI image compiles its API origin at build time; pointing it at a
  different server means rebuilding with `NEXT_PUBLIC_CAIRN_API`.
- Performance figures are measured on Apple silicon; other hardware is
  unmeasured.

Full detail in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Vellixia/Cairn/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
